The human eye has a massive "dynamic range"—the ability to see details in very bright areas and very dark areas simultaneously. Cameras have a much narrower dynamic range. They must choose to expose for the bright areas (making dark areas pitch black) or expose for the dark areas (making bright areas completely white).

*   **How it works:** If you place bright, visible spotlights inside the window, pointing outward toward the street, you force the camera to make an exposure choice. *   **How it works:** Retroreflective materials (like the silver tape on high-visibility construction vests or certain types of projection screens) are designed to bounce light directly back at the source. If a camera flash goes off, the material bounces the intense light straight back into the camera lens. The camera will expose for this massive burst of light, plunging the rest of the window into total darkness. To a human walking by without a flashlight, the material just looks like normal gray fabric or tape.
